message.reasoning_content:
The workload: b ≈ 1.125*u + tiny noise, so residual is tiny relative to b — cancellation risk. float32 kernel computes b - alpha*u where alpha in fp32. Reference uses float64 (with recentring allowed). The key risk: fp32 cancellation error in residual could be amplified after normalization; tolerance is 1% relative to unit-norm reference, so error ~ ||residual_err|| / ||residual||. Need to estimate: b values ~1, noise 1e-5, so residual norm ~1e-5*sqrt(32)~5.7e-5. fp32 error in computing b - alpha*u: alpha fp32 rounding of 1.125 (exactly representable actually), u fp32 exact, b fp32 exact. If alpha computed accurately ≈1.125 (1.125 exact in fp32!), then residual = b - 1.125*u computed in fp32 with rounding ~1e-7*|b|. So error/residual norm could be ~1e-7/1e-5 ~ 1%+ → borderline! Great risk to flag. Also second loop recomputes residual identically; tl.arange(0,N) with N=32 fine.
